title: Two letters that ask you to stop and listen.
subtitle: Ha Mim opens the surah of the smoke
then: This surah came in Makkah, at a time when Quraysh were growing more hostile to the Prophet ﷺ. It opens with two letters, Ha and Mim. {idea}Their meaning is known to Allah.{/idea} What they do for the listener is clear: they halt the ear before the message begins.
now: You open the app between two notifications. Your thumb is already looking for the next thing. Two letters you cannot explain sit at the top of the page. {idea}Let them slow you down for one breath.{/idea}
old: If I cannot explain a word, I can skip past it.
new: Some words are there to make me stop, not to be decoded.
try: Before you read today, put the phone face down for five seconds, then begin.

title: An oath by the Book that makes things clear.
subtitle: Why Allah swears by His own clear Book
then: The people of Makkah claimed the Quran was made up by the Prophet ﷺ. The surah answers by swearing by the Book itself. {idea}The Book that makes things clear is its own witness{/idea} to where it came from.
now: Someone in a group chat says it is just an old book, written by people. You have heard it and never really checked. {idea}The answer it gives is: read me and see how clear I am.{/idea}
old: I need outside proof before I take this Book seriously.
new: The Book asks to be weighed by its own clarity first.
try: Read one short passage slowly today and note one thing it made clear to you.

title: The Quran came down on a blessed night.
subtitle: Laylatul-Qadr, and why the warning is a gift
then: Ibn Kathir explains the blessed night as Laylatul-Qadr in Ramadan. Makkah treated the message as {trap}a disaster that had landed on them{/trap}. The verse says the hour it came was {reward}blessed{/reward}, and its warning tells people what is good for them and what harms them.
now: The doctor tells you your blood sugar is high. It ruins your afternoon. Years later you realise {reward}that appointment saved you{/reward}. A warning that arrives in time is a kindness, even when it stings.
old: A warning is bad news I would rather not hear.
new: A warning that comes in time is a mercy that came early.
try: Think of one warning you got this year and brushed off. Give it a second look.

title: On that night the year's matters are set out.
subtitle: Decrees that are wise and firm
then: Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn Umar, Mujahid and others that on this night {idea}the decrees of the coming year are passed to the angelic scribes{/idea}: life span, provision, and what will happen. The word hakim means decided and firm.
now: January. You buy a new planner and fill in goals, a budget, a holiday. You feel in charge. {idea}Plan anyway, but hold it lightly.{/idea} Your year is already known to the One who is wise.
old: My year will go the way I plan it.
new: I plan, and my year rests in a wise decree I can trust.
try: Look at one plan for this month and add a quiet in sha Allah to it.

title: Every matter comes as a command from Him.
subtitle: Nothing happens outside His leave and knowledge
then: Ibn Kathir says everything that happens and the revelation He sends down {idea}all comes by His command, by His leave and with His knowledge{/idea}. Sending messengers to people was an urgent need, and He met it.
now: The bus is late, the job offer comes, the test result is fine. You call it luck. {idea}The verse calls it a command that was sent.{/idea} That changes how you thank and how you wait.
old: Most of what happens to me is random.
new: What reaches me was sent, and guidance was sent too.
try: When something good happens today, say alhamdulillah instead of lucky.

title: The message is mercy from the One who hears.
subtitle: Revelation as care, not burden
then: Makkah was in the grip of a famine when this surah came, and its leaders wanted relief. The verse names the revelation itself as {reward}a mercy from your Lord{/reward}, sent by One who hears and knows.
now: You read a verse that asks something of you and feel the weight first. Picture a parent writing a note before a long trip: eat well, lock the door. {reward}That note is love written down.{/reward}
old: Religious guidance is mostly a list of demands.
new: The guidance is mercy from One who heard what I needed.
try: Pick one instruction you find heavy and ask: how could this be care for me?

title: Lord of everything, if you want certainty.
subtitle: The Sender of the Book owns the heavens and earth
then: Ibn Kathir says the One who sent the Quran is {idea}the Lord, Creator and Sovereign of the heavens and the earth{/idea} and all between them. The verse adds: if you have real certainty. The people of Makkah admitted Allah created all this, yet doubted His Book.
now: You believe Allah made the sky. You also check your horoscope app, just for fun. {trap}Certainty in one place, doubt in another.{/trap} The verse asks you to let the first certainty reach the second.
old: I believe in Allah, but I am not sure about the details.
new: If He owns everything, then His Book deserves the same certainty.
try: Go outside tonight, look up at the sky for a minute, and remember who sent the Book.

title: Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers.
subtitle: The One who gives life and takes it
then: Quraysh held on to idols because their ancestors did. The verse answers: {idea}He is your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers{/idea}. The ancestors were His creation too, and He gave them life and took it.
now: A family tradition you keep because "we always did it this way." Your grandmother's photo on the wall. {idea}The One who gave her life gave you yours.{/idea} Loyalty to her includes returning to Him.
old: Keeping family ways is how I honour those before me.
new: The truest link to my forefathers is the Lord we share.
try: Make a short dua for one grandparent or ancestor by name today.

title: They play around inside their doubt.
subtitle: Treating certain truth as a game
then: After all that clarity, the verse says the idolaters {trap}play about in doubt{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says the certain truth had come to them, but they doubted it and did not believe. Their doubt was not a search. It was a way of passing time.
now: You keep a few big questions open for years. You never sit down to look into them. You scroll instead. {trap}Doubt you never work on becomes a game you play.{/trap}
old: Staying undecided is the honest, safe position.
new: Doubt I never look into is just a way of not deciding.
try: Write down one question about faith you have carried for years. Find one honest answer this week.

title: Watch for the day the sky brings smoke.
subtitle: The sign that gives the surah its name
then: Ibn Mas'ud said Quraysh, stubborn against Islam, were struck with years of famine. {trap}They were so hungry that they saw only smoke between them and the sky.{/trap} Other reports, Ibn Kathir notes, make the Smoke one of the signs still awaited before the Hour.
now: You watch a news clip of wildfire haze over a city, people in masks. You talk about it and then move on. {idea}The verse says: watch.{/idea} Signs are for waking up, not just for discussing.
old: Big signs are for debating what they mean.
new: A sign is meant to change me, whatever its timing.
try: Next time hard news shakes you, pause and ask what it is asking of you.

title: It covers everyone. This is a painful punishment.
subtitle: When no one can stand outside it

row.title: it covers people
sub: so I check my own state

then: Ibn Kathir points out that the verse says {trap}covering mankind{/trap}, which he takes to mean something all will see, not only Makkah's hungry. The words this is a painful torment are said to them as a rebuke.
now: A storm alert flashes on every phone in the city at once. Nobody is "too important" for it. {idea}What touches everyone makes you look at yourself first{/idea}, not at who deserves it.
old: Warnings like this are about other people.
new: When it covers everyone, the only question is how I am standing.
try: Ask Allah tonight, in your own words, for safety for yourself and the people around you.

title: Remove it, Lord, and we will believe.
subtitle: Promises made only under pressure

row.title: before the crisis
sub: when it is still a choice

then: Ibn Kathir says when disbelievers witness Allah's punishment, {trap}they ask for it to be removed and promise to believe{/trap}. He links it to those who will wish to be sent back so they would not deny again.
now: The hospital corridor at 2 a.m. You promise: if they pull through, I will pray every prayer. Then they pull through. {idea}The verse asks what your faith looks like on an ordinary Tuesday.{/idea}
old: I will get serious about faith when I really need it.
new: Faith that only appears in a crisis is a bargain, not a bond.
try: Recall one promise you made to Allah in a hard moment. Keep a small piece of it today.

title: How can a reminder help them now?
subtitle: The clear Messenger had already come
then: The people asking for relief and promising faith {reward}had already had a clear Messenger ﷺ among them{/reward}, explaining things plainly. The verse asks how a reminder can help someone who {trap}turned from it when it came{/trap}.
now: You keep saying you will listen when someone explains it properly. Meanwhile the lecture link sits unopened in your messages. {idea}The reminder is already in your pocket.{/idea}
old: I would act if the message were clearer.
new: The message was clear. I was not listening.
try: Open one reminder someone sent you weeks ago and actually watch or read it.

title: They turned away and called him tutored and mad.
subtitle: Labels that make listening unnecessary
then: Quraysh did not answer the message. {trap}They turned away and attached labels to the Messenger ﷺ{/trap}: someone taught him, he is mad. Once a label sticks, nobody has to think about the words.
now: A colleague raises a fair point in a meeting. Someone mutters "she always complains" and the room moves on. {trap}A label is the fastest way to stop listening.{/trap}
old: I know what kind of person they are, so I can ignore them.
new: Labelling a speaker is often how I avoid a true message.
try: Next time you want to dismiss someone, repeat their point back to yourself fairly first.

title: The pain lifted a little, and they went back.
subtitle: Relief that ends the promise
then: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ to pray for rain for Mudar, who were dying. He prayed and the rain came. Ibn Mas'ud said {trap}when they were granted ease, they returned to their former state{/trap}. The verse had already said it: We will lift it a little, and you will go back.
now: The scan comes back clear. The debt is paid. In a month, the habits you swore off are back. {idea}Ease is the moment the promise is really tested.{/idea}
old: Once things get better, I can relax.
new: Relief is the real test of what I promised in the hard days.
try: Think of one thing that got easier recently and thank Allah with one concrete act.

title: The day of the great seizing will come.
subtitle: Respite does not mean it was forgotten
then: After the respite, Allah warned of {trap}a day of the great seizing{/trap}. Ibn Mas'ud said it was the day of Badr. Ibn Abbas said it is the Day of Resurrection, which Ibn Kathir calls the apparent meaning. Either way, the delay was time given, not a pardon.
now: You did something wrong years ago and nothing happened. You almost forgot. {idea}Quiet years are not a verdict. They are time to set it right{/idea} while you still can.
old: If nothing happened, it must not have mattered.
new: Delay is time given to me to come back, not a sign it was ignored.
try: Make one thing right that you have let slide because no one noticed.

title: Pharaoh's people were tested before Makkah was.
subtitle: A noble messenger came to them first
then: Right after warning Quraysh, the surah turns to an older story. Ibn Kathir says {idea}before these idolaters, Allah tested the people of Pharaoh{/idea}, the Copts of Egypt. A noble messenger came to them: Musa, the one Allah spoke to.
now: You think your situation is new: new pressures, new excuses. Then you read an old story and see yourself in it. {idea}The test is old. Only the clothes change.{/idea}
old: My circumstances are too different for old stories to apply.
new: The same test repeats: a clear message arrives, and I choose.
try: Read the story of Musa and Pharaoh this week and note one line that fits your life.

title: Hand over the servants of Allah to me.
subtitle: People are not property to keep
then: Musa's first words to Pharaoh were a demand: {idea}deliver to me the servants of Allah{/idea}. Ibn Kathir links it to the plea to let the Children of Israel go and not torment them. Musa added that he was {reward}a messenger worthy of trust{/reward}.
now: A manager who acts like he owns your evenings. A parent who treats a grown child as a possession. Or you, with someone under your authority. {idea}Everyone you have power over is Allah's servant first.{/idea}
old: The people under my authority are mine to manage as I like.
new: The people under me belong to Allah. I only hold a trust.
try: Think of one person you have authority over and ease one demand you make of them today.

title: Do not rise up against Allah.
subtitle: Arrogance toward clear proof
then: Musa told Pharaoh not to exalt himself against Allah. Ibn Kathir explains it as: {trap}do not be too arrogant to follow His signs{/trap}. Musa came with {idea}clear and obvious proof{/idea}.
now: Your teenager shows you that you were wrong about something. The facts are right there on the screen. You feel your face go hot. {trap}It is not the proof you are resisting. It is losing.{/trap}
old: I just need better evidence before I change my mind.
new: Often the evidence is clear and my pride is the problem.
try: Admit one small thing you were wrong about today, out loud, to someone.

title: I seek refuge in my Lord and yours.
subtitle: Facing threats by turning to Allah
then: Musa expected harm. Ibn Abbas said the stoning meant {trap}a verbal assault, insults{/trap}; Qatadah took it literally. Musa did not threaten back. He {idea}sought refuge with Allah, who created him and them{/idea}.
now: The comments under your post turn nasty. You start typing something sharp. {idea}Stop and say: I seek refuge in Allah.{/idea} Notice it is their Lord too.
old: When people attack me, I have to defend myself with words.
new: When attacked, I can turn first to the One who made us both.
try: Next time someone insults you, say a'udhu billah before you reply, or instead of replying.

title: If you will not believe me, leave me be.
subtitle: Stepping away in peace
then: Ibn Kathir explains Musa's words as: {idea}let us leave one another alone and live in peace until Allah judges between us{/idea}. He had delivered the message. He did not chase or force.
now: The family dinner where the same argument starts again. You have said your piece many times. {idea}You can stop and leave it with Allah{/idea} without slamming any door.
old: If they will not accept it, I have to keep pushing.
new: Once I have said it clearly, I can step back in peace.
try: Pick one argument you keep restarting and decide not to bring it up this week.

title: After long patience, Musa called on his Lord.
subtitle: When a people persist in wrongdoing
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}Musa stayed among them a long time{/idea}, until the proof had been established. It only made them more stubborn. Then he called on his Lord: {trap}these are a criminal people{/trap}. His prayer was answered.
now: You have tried for years to fix a situation at work: emails, meetings, patience. Nothing changes. {idea}There comes a point where you hand it to Allah in dua{/idea}, honestly, and let Him decide.
old: Making dua about a hard situation means I gave up.
new: After real effort, handing it to Allah is the next step, not surrender.
try: Name one problem you have worked on for a long time and make a sincere dua about it tonight.

title: Leave by night. You will be followed.
subtitle: Moving forward with eyes open
then: Allah commanded Musa to bring the Children of Israel out {idea}without Pharaoh's command or permission{/idea}. They were told in advance: {trap}you will be pursued{/trap}. The danger was named before they took a step.
now: You are leaving a bad situation: a toxic job, a harmful friendship, a habit. You know it will come after you. {idea}Being told it is hard is part of being guided.{/idea}
old: If this is the right path, it should feel easy.
new: The right path can come with a warning that it will be hard.
try: Name one hard thing you know is coming if you change, and plan one way through it.

title: Leave the sea as it is. Keep moving.
subtitle: Not closing the door yourself
then: Ibn Kathir says after crossing, {idea}Musa wanted to strike the sea{/idea} so it would close behind them. Allah told him to leave it still and divided and keep moving. {reward}He gave him good news{/reward} that the army would be drowned.
now: You keep checking the lock, rereading the email, planning every backup. You cannot rest until every gap is closed. {idea}Sometimes the command is: do your part and keep walking.{/idea}
old: I am only safe when I have controlled every risk myself.
new: I do what I am told and trust Allah with the gap behind me.
try: Choose one worry you keep rechecking and leave it alone for one day.

title: So many gardens and springs, left behind.
subtitle: What they could not take with them
then: The surah counts what Pharaoh's people left. Ibn Kathir says the springs were their rivers and wells. {trap}All of it was taken away in a single morning.{/trap}
now: You walk through a house sale after someone died. Their good chairs, their garden tools, price stickers on everything. {trap}So much, left behind.{/trap} One day it will be your stickers.
old: What I build up here is mine to keep.
new: Everything I own I will leave behind, so I hold it lightly.
try: Give away one thing you own but no longer use.

title: Fields of crops and fine homes, gone.
subtitle: The dwellings they were proud of
then: The list continues with crops and noble places. Ibn Kathir says these were {reward}fine dwellings and beautiful places{/reward}; Mujahid said elevated places. {trap}They lived high, and lost it all.{/trap}
now: You scroll home tours online, saving pictures of kitchens. You start measuring your worth by your square metres. {idea}A home is a place to pass through well{/idea}, not a monument.
old: A fine home shows that I have made it.
new: A fine home is a blessing on the road, not the place I end up.
try: Thank Allah for one specific thing about the place you live today.

title: The comfort they enjoyed so much.
subtitle: Delight that forgot its Giver

row.title: comfort
sub: eat and wear as they liked

then: Ibn Kathir describes {reward}a life where they could eat what they wanted and wear what they liked{/reward}, with wealth, glory and power. Then, he says, {trap}all of that was taken away in a single morning{/trap}.
now: Friday night: a good meal, a comfy sofa, a show you love. Nothing wrong with any of it. {idea}The question is whether the comfort ever reminds you of who gave it.{/idea}
old: My comforts are just the normal life I deserve.
new: Every comfort is a gift that can end, so I enjoy it with thanks.
try: At your next meal, pause before the first bite and thank Allah for one detail of it.

title: So it was, and others inherited it.
subtitle: The oppressed received what the oppressors left
then: Ibn Kathir says the other people who inherited it were {idea}the Children of Israel{/idea}, the very people Pharaoh had enslaved. Those who had nothing received what the proud left behind.
now: The office you work in had a different boss ten years ago, and will have another in ten more. {idea}Every position you hold is on loan.{/idea} Use it while it is yours.
old: Whoever holds power now will keep it.
new: Everything is passed on. Allah decides who holds it next.
try: Use one privilege you have today to help someone who has less of it.

title: Neither sky nor earth wept for them.
subtitle: Leaving no trace of good behind
then: Ibn Abbas was asked whether sky and earth weep for anyone. He said yes: {reward}every person has a gate in the heavens{/reward} through which provision descends and deeds rise, and it weeps when a believer dies, as does the place he prayed. {trap}Pharaoh's people left no such trace.{/trap}
now: Think of the corner of your room where you pray, the bus stop where you make dhikr. {idea}Those spots would notice if you were gone.{/idea} Is there a place on earth that would miss you?
old: I will be remembered for what I built and achieved.
new: The places where I prayed and did good are what will miss me.
try: Pray two units somewhere new today, so one more patch of earth knows you.

title: Allah saved the Children of Israel from humiliation.
subtitle: Rescue from forced, degrading labour
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah reminds them how He saved them from {trap}their humiliation and subjugation at the hands of Pharaoh{/trap}, when they were forced to do menial tasks. The rescue is told in His words: {idea}We saved.{/idea}
now: You remember a year that crushed you: the debt, the illness, the boss who belittled you. You got through it. {idea}Name who really carried you out.{/idea}
old: I got myself out of my worst times.
new: Allah brought me out of my worst times, even through my effort.
try: Write down one hard period you survived and thank Allah for it by name.

title: Pharaoh was arrogant and went beyond every limit.
subtitle: A man with a foolish opinion of himself
then: Ibn Kathir says Pharaoh was {trap}proud and stubborn{/trap}, one who exalted himself in the land, and that he {trap}held a foolish opinion of himself{/trap}. The tyranny started with how he saw himself.
now: Being the one who always knows best in the family chat. Never asking for help at work because you are "above it." {idea}The Pharaoh in a story starts small in a person.{/idea}
old: Arrogance is the sin of powerful people, not mine.
new: Arrogance starts as an inflated picture of myself, at any size.
try: Ask someone for help with one thing today that you would normally do alone.

title: Chosen with knowledge above the people of their time.
subtitle: Being chosen is a responsibility
then: Mujahid said they were {idea}chosen above those among whom they lived{/idea}. Qatadah said above the people of their own time, and that in every period some are chosen above others. Ibn Kathir compares it to Musa and Maryam being chosen above people of their time.
now: You were given something others were not: a good school, a believing family, a skill. {idea}That is a choice made with knowledge, for a reason.{/idea} It is not a ranking to boast about.
old: What I was given makes me better than others.
new: What I was given is a trust chosen for me, with a test inside it.
try: List one advantage you were born with and use it for someone else today.

title: Signs were given to them, and with them a clear test.
subtitle: Miracles also reveal who will follow
then: Ibn Kathir says the signs were {reward}clear proofs and extraordinary evidence{/reward}, and the trial in them was {idea}an obvious test to show who would be guided by it{/idea}. Being shown more meant being asked more.
now: Your prayer for a job was answered. Your child recovered. You saw it. {idea}Now the answer is watching what you do next.{/idea} A blessing seen is a question asked.
old: If I saw a clear sign, faith would be easy.
new: Every sign I see is also a test of how I respond.
try: Recall one dua that was answered and do one act today that shows you noticed.

title: Now listen to what these people are saying.
subtitle: The surah returns to Makkah's denial
then: After Pharaoh's story, the surah turns back: {trap}these people are saying{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says Allah here denounces the idolaters for denying the Resurrection, believing there is nothing after this life.
now: You finish a documentary about an empire that fell and feel wise. Then the narrator turns to the camera and asks about you. {idea}The story was always pointed at the listener.{/idea}
old: Stories of past nations are about them.
new: Every old story ends by turning to look at me.
try: After you read a story in the Quran today, ask: which character am I most like?

title: There is only our first death, they said.
subtitle: Living as if nothing comes after
then: Ibn Kathir says they believed {trap}there is nothing after this life and no life or resurrection after death{/trap}. They based it on the fact that their forefathers had died and not come back.
now: Few people say out loud there is nothing after death. But you can live as if it were true: plan for retirement in detail and the grave not at all. {idea}What you prepare for shows what you believe.{/idea}
old: I believe in the Hereafter, so this verse is not about me.
new: If I never prepare for after death, I am living their belief.
try: Spend five minutes today on something only the Hereafter will pay you for.

title: Bring back our fathers, if you are truthful.
subtitle: A demand that misunderstands the promise
then: They said: if resurrection is true, bring back our forefathers. Ibn Kathir calls this {trap}false evidence and a specious argument{/trap}. {idea}The resurrection will happen on the Day of Judgement{/idea}, when this world has ended, not in it.
now: You hear someone say: nobody ever came back to tell us. It sounds clever. {idea}No one was promised a return here.{/idea} The promise was always for a Day after.
old: If it were real, someone would have come back to show us.
new: The raising was promised for after this world, not inside it.
try: Visit or remember a relative's grave and make dua for them by name.

title: Are they better than the people of Tubba'?
subtitle: Strong nations before them also fell
then: Tubba' was the title of the kings of Himyar, also called Saba'. Ibn Kathir says {trap}Allah destroyed them and scattered them{/trap} for denying the Resurrection. He notes the Prophet ﷺ said he did not know whether Tubba' himself was a prophet, and forbade reviling him.
now: You think your security is solid: a good salary, a strong passport, healthy parents. {idea}Stronger people than you trusted the same things.{/idea} What protects you is how you live.
old: We are stronger than those who fell before.
new: Strength never saved anyone. Their deeds decided their end.
try: Think of one way you rely on your own strength and turn it into a dua.

title: We did not create all this in play.
subtitle: The world was made with wisdom
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah here tells of {idea}His justice, and that He is far above play, folly and falsehood{/idea}. He links it to the verse: did you think We created you in play, and that you would not be brought back to Us?
now: A late night, you scroll and think: what is any of this for? The commute, the bills, the same week again. {idea}None of it was made for nothing.{/idea} Your ordinary day is part of a purpose.
old: Most of life is just filler between the big moments.
new: Nothing in creation is filler, and that includes my ordinary day.
try: Pick one routine task today and do it with a clear intention for Allah.

title: Created in truth, though most do not know.
subtitle: Purpose that many never notice
then: The verse continues the last one: creation was made {idea}in truth{/idea}, for a purpose. Ibn Kathir links it to the Day when Allah will judge between all creatures. Yet {trap}most of them do not know{/trap}.
now: Everyone around you lives for the weekend, the promotion, the next trip. It feels normal because it is common. {idea}Common is not the same as true.{/idea}
old: If most people do not think about purpose, I do not need to either.
new: The purpose is true even when most people around me ignore it.
try: Ask yourself one question tonight: what was I created for? Write one sentence.

title: The Day of Sorting is everyone's appointment.
subtitle: First and last, all gathered
then: Ibn Kathir says this is the Day of Resurrection, when {idea}Allah will judge between all creatures{/idea}. The time appointed for all of them means He will gather {idea}the first and the last of them{/idea}.
now: Your calendar has a dentist appointment you cannot move. You plan the whole week around it. {idea}There is one appointment already booked for you that no one can cancel.{/idea}
old: Judgement is something far off that I can think about later.
new: The Day is an appointment already set, with my name on it.
try: Add one small good deed to your calendar for tomorrow, like it is an appointment.

title: No relative can help another on that Day.
subtitle: Kinship cannot carry you
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}no relative will be able to help another{/trap}, and no help will come from outside. He links it to the verse that no friend will ask about a friend, even though they see one another.
now: You have always had someone: a parent who signs the form, a brother who lends money, a friend who covers. {idea}On that Day, you stand on your own.{/idea} Love them now, and prepare for yourself.
old: My family will always be there to back me up.
new: My family is a gift here. There, I carry my own deeds.
try: Do one good deed today on your own account, without anyone else involved.

title: Except those on whom Allah has mercy.
subtitle: The one exception on that Day
then: After saying no one can help anyone, the verse opens one door. Ibn Kathir says {reward}nothing will be of any avail that Day except the mercy of Allah{/reward}. He is the All-Mighty, {reward}with immense mercy{/reward}.
now: The waiting room before a big result. Nobody can change it for you. Then one sentence lifts it: except whom Allah has mercy on. {reward}That door is open, and you can knock now.{/reward}
old: If no one can help me then, the Day is only frightening.
new: When every other help is gone, His mercy is still there.
try: Ask Allah for His mercy today in your own words, for yourself and one other person.

title: The tree of Zaqqum is named.
subtitle: The surah turns to those who denied the meeting
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah here tells {trap}how He will punish the disbelievers who deny the meeting with Him{/trap}. Some commentators applied it to Abu Jahl; Ibn Kathir says he is included, but it is not only about him.
now: A road sign shows a sharp bend ahead. It is not there to frighten you. {idea}It is there so you slow down in time.{/idea} Descriptions of the Fire work the same way.
old: Verses about the Fire are only meant to frighten.
new: The warning is described so I can steer away while there is time.
try: Name one habit you know is heading the wrong way and make one small turn today.

title: It is the food of the one who sinned.
subtitle: What a life of wrongdoing feeds on
then: Ibn Kathir says the sinner here is one who {trap}sinned by words and deeds{/trap}. Abu ad-Darda' corrected a man who misheard the word as orphan: say {trap}the food of the evildoer{/trap}, meaning he will have no other food.
now: The shows you binge, the gossip you swallow in the group chat, the money you earn in a grey way. {idea}What you feed your soul now is a kind of food too.{/idea}
old: What I consume day to day does not really affect me.
new: What I take in now shapes where I end up.
try: Skip one thing today you know feeds the worst in you, and replace it with something good.

title: Like dregs of oil, it churns inside.
subtitle: Food that harms instead of nourishing
then: Ibn Kathir explains the word as {trap}like the dregs of oil{/trap}. It boils in the bellies {trap}because of its heat and rancidity{/trap}. It is food that gives nothing and only hurts.
now: The angry message you sent felt good for ten seconds. Then it sat in your stomach all night. {idea}Some things taste fine going down and churn afterwards.{/idea}
old: If it feels good now, it cannot be that bad.
new: Wrong that feels good now can turn bitter inside me.
try: Before you react today, ask: how will this feel in an hour? Then choose.

title: Boiling like scalding water.
subtitle: No cooling, no comfort

row.title: seek refuge now
sub: ask to be kept from it

then: The image completes the last verse: the food boils inside {trap}like the boiling of scalding water{/trap}. Ibn Kathir keeps the explanation short. The picture is meant to be enough.
now: You pull your hand back from a kettle without thinking. Your body knows to avoid harm. {idea}The verse asks your heart to learn the same reflex.{/idea}
old: I can deal with these warnings some other time.
new: My heart should flinch from the Fire the way my hand flinches from heat.
try: Ask Allah tonight to protect you and your family from the Fire.

title: Seize him and drag him to the middle.
subtitle: The proud are taken without a say
then: The order is given to the keepers of Hell. Mujahid said it means {trap}take him and push him{/trap}, into the middle of the Fire. The one who did as he pleased now has no say at all.
now: Right now you decide when to wake, what to eat, whether to pray. That freedom feels permanent. {idea}It is the window in which choices still count.{/idea}
old: I will always be in charge of my own choices.
new: My freedom to choose is a window, and it closes.
try: Use your freedom today to choose one good thing you have been putting off.

title: Then pour over his head the boiling torment.
subtitle: A sober picture of what denial reaches
then: The punishment continues: {trap}pour over his head the torment of boiling water{/trap}. Ibn Kathir links it to a similar verse in Surah al-Hajj and adds a short prayer: {reward}may Allah protect us from that{/reward}.
now: You want to scroll past this verse quickly. That is fine to feel. {reward}Do what Ibn Kathir did: stop and ask Allah to protect you.{/reward}
old: Hard verses are best skipped.
new: Hard verses are a cue to pause and ask for protection.
try: When you reach a verse about the Fire, stop and say: Allah, protect me from it.

title: Taste it, you who thought yourself mighty and noble.
subtitle: The status he claimed, said back to him
then: The keepers of Hell say this {trap}by way of ridicule and rebuke{/trap}. Ibn Abbas said it means: {trap}you are neither mighty nor generous{/trap}. The titles he carried in this world are handed back to him empty.
now: The job title on your email signature. The family name people respect. The way the room quiets when you speak. {idea}None of these titles is checked on the Day. Only what you did is.{/idea}
old: My standing among people says something about my worth.
new: Titles end at the grave. My deeds are my only rank.
try: Do one humble task today you would normally leave to someone else.

title: This is what you used to doubt.
subtitle: The doubt from verse nine, answered
then: The surah began by saying they {trap}play about in doubt{/trap}. Here it closes the loop: {trap}this is what you used to doubt{/trap}. Ibn Kathir links it to: this is the Fire which you used to deny, is this magic, or do you not see?
now: You put off reading the letter from the bank because you suspect what it says. Not opening it does not change the number. {idea}Doubt only delays the moment you see it.{/idea}
old: As long as I am not sure, I do not have to act.
new: My doubt will end either way. Better it ends now, by choice.
try: Settle one question you have been doubting by asking someone knowledgeable this week.

title: The mindful will be in a place of safety.
subtitle: After the warning, the other side
then: Ibn Kathir says when Allah describes the doomed, He follows with the blessed, which is why the Quran is called oft-repeated. {reward}The place of security{/reward} is Paradise, safe from death, from fear of leaving it, and from {reward}every worry, grief, terror and exhaustion{/reward}.
now: Even on your best holiday, part of you counts the days left. Even when the bills are paid, you think of next month. {reward}Picture a safety with no countdown.{/reward}
old: Peace never lasts, so I should not expect it.
new: There is a safety coming that never runs out.
try: Next time worry hits, say: Allah, make me among the people of the safe place.

title: Among gardens and springs.
subtitle: The exact opposite of Zaqqum
then: Ibn Kathir says this is {reward}in direct contrast to the state of the doomed{/reward}, who have Zaqqum and boiling water. The same words were used for what Pharaoh's people {trap}left behind{/trap}. Here they are given and kept.
now: The garden you are saving for, the house by the water you dream of. {idea}The surah shows the same picture twice: one lost in a morning, one kept forever.{/idea}
old: I want gardens and springs here, now.
new: The gardens worth wanting are the ones that are never left behind.
try: Sit by a plant, tree or running tap for a minute and ask Allah for the gardens that last.

title: Dressed in fine silk, facing one another.
subtitle: No one sits with his back to another
then: Ibn Kathir explains sundus as {reward}the finest silk{/reward} and istabraq as silk woven with shiny threads. Facing each other means {reward}sitting on thrones where none of them sits with his back to anyone else{/reward}.
now: A wedding where two cousins have not spoken in years sit at tables turned away. Everyone feels it. {reward}In Paradise no one turns their back.{/reward} You can start that here.
old: Some people I simply will not face again.
new: The people of Paradise sit face to face, so I can begin practising now.
try: Send a short, kind message to one person you have been avoiding.

title: Joined to companions of rare beauty.
subtitle: A gift on top of every gift
then: Ibn Kathir says this will be {reward}a gift in addition to{/reward} the wives given to them. He cites the verse: {reward}is there any reward for good other than good?{/reward}
now: You do a good deed and wonder if it even counted. A small charity, a patient reply. {reward}Allah's answer to good is more good{/reward}, far beyond what you gave.
old: My small good deeds will barely register.
new: Allah returns good with good, and then adds more.
try: Do one quiet good deed today and trust it is fully seen.

title: Asking for any fruit, in perfect security.
subtitle: Plenty with no fear of running out
then: Ibn Kathir says whatever fruit they ask for is brought, and {reward}they have the security of knowing this supply will never come to an end or be withheld{/reward}. The safety is part of the pleasure.
now: Payday, the fridge is full, and still you check your banking app twice. Even plenty here comes with worry. {reward}There, the asking and the receiving come without fear.{/reward}
old: Having more would finally stop me worrying.
new: Only in Paradise does plenty come with no worry at all.
try: Share some fruit or food with someone today and enjoy it without rushing.

title: No more death, only the first one.
subtitle: Life that does not end
then: Earlier, deniers said there is only our first death. Here the believers {reward}never taste death there except the first death{/reward}. Ibn Kathir cites the hadith that death will be slaughtered and it will be said: {reward}O people of Paradise, eternal, no more death.{/reward}
now: A funeral, a phone call at night. Every loss reminds you that everyone you love will die. {reward}This verse promises a life where that call never comes.{/reward}
old: Death will always be the thing that takes everything.
new: For the believer, the first death is the last one.
try: Make dua for someone you have lost, asking Allah to reunite you where there is no death.

title: A bounty from your Lord, the great success.
subtitle: Entered by His grace, not by our deeds alone
then: Ibn Kathir cites the hadith: {idea}work and strive, and know that no one enters Paradise by virtue of his deeds{/idea}. They asked: not even you? The Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}not even me, unless Allah covers me with His mercy and grace{/reward}.
now: You keep a mental tally: prayers prayed, charity given, fasts kept. Some days it feels like enough, some days nothing. {reward}Keep working, but lean on His grace, not on your tally.{/reward}
old: If I do enough, I will have earned Paradise.
new: I work hard, and my hope rests on His grace.
try: After your next prayer, say: Allah, accept it by Your mercy, not by its worth.

title: We made it easy in your tongue, so they remember.
subtitle: A clear Book, made to be understood
then: The surah opened with the clear Book and closes with it. Ibn Kathir says Allah made the Quran {idea}easy, plain and clear{/idea}, in the most eloquent language, so they may understand. {trap}Yet some still stubbornly go against it.{/trap}
now: You have told yourself for years that the Quran is too hard to understand without a teacher. Meanwhile you understand complex phone contracts. {idea}It was made easy for you. Open it.{/idea}
old: The Quran is too hard for someone like me.
new: It was made easy on purpose, so I could remember.
try: Read the translation of one short surah today, start to finish.

title: So wait. They are waiting too.
subtitle: A calm close to a surah of warning
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah says this to His Messenger ﷺ, {reward}consoling him and promising him victory{/reward}. They will come to know whose word prevails, for victory belongs to the Messengers and those who believe. The surah began with watch, and ends with wait.
now: You are doing the right thing and the people around you are waiting for you to fail. The colleague who rolls his eyes. The relative who says it will not last. {reward}Wait calmly. You are not waiting alone.{/reward}
old: When people expect me to fail, I have to prove them wrong now.
new: I can wait in calm trust. Allah has promised to help those who believe.
try: Think of one good thing you started that others doubt, and keep it up today without arguing.
